$comment: downshift routing matrix. Point `executors` at the models you actually have — `route.py add` writes the entries for you. Everything else is policy you probably want to keep.
$cost_note: On a subscription you do not pay per token, you consume a window. Every executor points at a pool (the subscription it draws on) and carries a relative weight. The pools are separate, and that is where the real saving lives.

policy.$family_note: Two roles, rename them to suit your stack: the judgement family is the one you trust with an ambiguous target and is never substituted away; the execution family takes fully specified work.

claude.window: 5h + weekly, shared by haiku/sonnet/opus and by claude.ai
claude.quota_source: manual: /usage in Claude Code. No reliable local source (issues 35992, 44328)
claude.reserve_why: above this, the Claude pool is kept for judgement, debugging and critical work

codex.reserve_why: above this, Codex is kept for multi-file implementation and critical second opinions

opencode.reserve_why: free: always used where the result is instantly verifiable

S1.name: lookup
S1.what: find, read, list, git log. No edit.

S2.name: mechanical
S2.what: deterministic edit that lint/typecheck/grep closes: rename, format, imports, docstrings, boilerplate.

S3.name: local
S3.what: small fix or helper in 1-2 files, cause already known, covered by an existing test.

M1.name: feature
M1.what: clear spec across 3-8 files, tests still to write. No judgement left open. The test does not exist yet, so verification is not free.

M2.name: debug
M2.what: red test or reproducible bug, but the cause still has to be found.

M3.name: refactor
M3.what: more than 8 files, or shared interfaces, with the target already decided.

C1.name: design
C1.what: ambiguous requirement, trade-offs, architecture, migration plan.

C2.name: critical
C2.what: auth, security, payments, data deletion, DB migrations, infra, production.

$weight_note: weight = how hard that model bites its own pool's quota, relative. It is not a price: it only breaks ties between two options inside the same pool.
